I've got 12 mu here in Quzhou and I've been farming it for 25 years, so I know what works. My wife and eldest son work at a factory in town, so it's mostly me and my younger son doing the farm work. That means I have to be realistic about labor. Cotton is my main money maker — I keep 9 mu in cotton because our soil is good for it and I've always done well with it. The other 3 mu I do wheat-maize rotation. The wheat is already in the ground from last fall, and after we harvest in early June we'll plant maize right away with no-tillage because there's no time to plow. For wheat, I use improved seed and rotary tillage, put down compound fertilizer as base and topdress urea at jointing — about 17 kg nitrogen per mu — and irrigate three times. I expect around 520 kg per mu. For cotton, I rotary till in April, plant improved Bt seed, spread about 60 kg of compound per mu before planting, irrigate three times, and spray pesticides about 5 times for bollworm and aphids. I should get about 300 kg of seed cotton per mu. For maize, I plant hybrid Denghai 605 right after wheat harvest, put compound in the row, irrigate twice, and expect about 480 kg per mu. Fertilizer is expensive this year but I learned in 2019 that cutting back costs more in lost yield, so I'd rather use a bit extra than risk it. The well pump costs electricity, so I only irrigate when the crops really need it.
